name: Lincoln Memorial
description: The great marble temple at the west end of the Mall, with the seated Lincoln and his two most famous speeches carved on the walls. The view east over the Reflecting Pool is the city's classic picture.
tips: Open 24 hours, every day. Rangers are on duty from 9:30 a.m. to 10 p.m.
Come back after dark: the memorial is lit and much quieter.
Nearest Metro: Foggy Bottom, about a 15 to 20 minute walk.

access.note: A wide flight of steps up the front. Ask a ranger about the accessible entrance.

name: Washington Monument

price.text: Free · $1 online booking fee per ticket

lead_time: Book ahead: tickets open online 30 days before at 10 a.m. Eastern, plus a day-before release.
description: The marble obelisk at the center of the Mall. An elevator takes about 70 seconds to the top, with views over the city, the river and Virginia.
tips: Free, but everyone 2 and older needs a timed ticket. Online tickets have a $1 booking fee.
Online tickets open 30 days ahead at 10 a.m. Eastern, with more released the day before. Make a recreation.gov account early.
Free same-day tickets at the Washington Monument Lodge on 15th Street from 8:45 a.m., while they last. Expect a line.
Closes one day a month for maintenance, on July 4 and Dec 25, and in high wind or storms. Check the alerts on nps.gov/wamo.
closed_note: Closed Dec 25 and one day a month for maintenance

access.note: The visit is by elevator. Waiting outside before your time can be cold and windy.

name: World War II and Vietnam Veterans Memorials
description: Two very different memorials a short walk apart: the fountains and granite pillars of the World War II Memorial, and the black wall of the Vietnam Veterans Memorial, cut into the ground with more than 58,000 names.
tips: Open 24 hours and free.
Walk them on the way from the Washington Monument to the Lincoln Memorial.

name: Tidal Basin memorials: MLK, FDR and Jefferson
description: Three memorials around the Tidal Basin: Martin Luther King Jr. carved from a block of granite, the outdoor rooms of the FDR Memorial, and the domed Jefferson Memorial across the water.
tips: Open 24 hours and free.
A walk around the water links all three. Allow an hour or more.
Beautiful at night, when the Jefferson Memorial is lit.

access.note: Flat but long. Cold and windy by the water in November.

name: The White House from Lafayette Square
description: See the north front from Lafayette Square, or the south front from the Ellipse. The White House Visitor Center nearby has exhibits and a short film.
tips: Tours for international visitors can only be requested through your embassy, well ahead, and are not guaranteed.
White House Visitor Center: 1450 Pennsylvania Avenue NW.
Security zones change often; follow the signs and the officers' directions.

name: National Air and Space Museum
lead_time: Reserve free timed passes before you go; same-day passes go fast.
description: The Wright Flyer, Apollo 11's command module and a huge gallery of aircraft and spacecraft. After a decade of renovation, its last galleries reopened in fall 2026.
tips: Free, but everyone needs a free timed-entry pass for the DC museum.
A limited batch of same-day passes is released online each morning at 8:30 a.m. Eastern.
Enter on Jefferson Drive, the National Mall side.
Open 10 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. daily except Dec 25.

name: National Museum of African American History and Culture
lead_time: Reserve free timed passes before you go.
description: A deeply moving museum that starts underground with the history of slavery and rises to music, sport and culture. Plan at least three hours.
tips: Free, but everyone of any age needs a free timed-entry pass.
Advance passes open 30 days ahead at 8 a.m. Eastern; same-day passes go online at 8:15 a.m.
Open 10 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Tuesday to Sunday, and noon to 5:30 p.m. on Monday. Closed Dec 25.
Start at the bottom, in the history galleries, then work your way up.

access.note: Step-free with elevators. The history galleries are crowded and emotionally heavy.

name: National Museum of Natural History
description: Dinosaurs, the Hope Diamond, a life-size whale and the ocean hall, under a great rotunda with an African elephant.
tips: Free, no pass needed.
Busiest at midday and on weekends; go at opening.

name: National Museum of American History
description: The Star-Spangled Banner that inspired the anthem, first ladies' gowns, presidents and pop culture. A good rainy-day museum.
tips: Free, no pass needed.

name: National Gallery of Art
description: Old masters in the West Building, including the only Leonardo da Vinci painting in the Americas, and modern art in the I. M. Pei East Building, linked by an underground walkway.
tips: Always free, no pass needed.
Open 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.
The Sculpture Garden next door is good for a break.

name: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum

price.text: Free · no pass needed Sept to Feb

description: The national memorial to the Holocaust, told through objects, photographs and survivors' voices. A powerful, demanding visit.
tips: Free. From September to February no pass is needed for the permanent exhibition.
Open daily 10 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Closed Yom Kippur and Dec 25.
Recommended for ages 11 and up; a separate exhibition, Daniel's Story, is for younger visitors.

access.note: Step-free. The permanent exhibition is graphic in places.

name: US Capitol tour
lead_time: Reserve a tour time online; same-day passes may be available.
description: A free guided tour of the Crypt, the Rotunda under the dome and National Statuary Hall, starting at the underground Capitol Visitor Center.
tips: Tours are free. Reserving a time is recommended, not required.
Open Monday to Saturday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The last tour starts at 3:20 p.m.
No reservation? Arrive early, and no later than 2:30 p.m., for a same-day pass.
Check the prohibited items list before you go; security is airport-style.
closed_note: Closed Sundays, Thanksgiving, Dec 25, Jan 1 and Inauguration Day

access.note: The visitor center and tour route are fully accessible.

name: Library of Congress
lead_time: Reserve a free timed ticket; same-day tickets go online at 9 a.m.
description: The Thomas Jefferson Building: a dazzling marble Great Hall, mosaics and a balcony view down into the domed Main Reading Room. Across the street from the Capitol.
tips: Free, but you need a free timed-entry ticket.
Tickets open 30 days ahead; free same-day tickets go online each day at 9 a.m. Eastern.
Open Tuesday to Saturday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., to 8 p.m. on Thursdays. Closed Sundays and Mondays.
Easy to pair with a Capitol tour: a tunnel links the two buildings.
closed_note: Closed Sundays, Mondays and some federal holidays

name: Eastern Market
description: A brick market hall from 1873 with butchers, bakers, cheese and a lunch counter. On weekends, farmers, craft and flea stalls fill the street outside.
tips: Indoor South Hall: Tuesday to Friday 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., Saturday 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., Sunday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
Weekends are the liveliest, with the outdoor stalls.
Eastern Market Metro is a short walk away.

food.note: Lots of choice: sandwiches, crab cakes, pastries and fruit.

name: Union Market
description: A big, bright food hall with more than 40 local vendors, from tacos and ramen to oysters and cookies. La Cosecha, a Latin American market, is across the street.
tips: Open Monday to Saturday 8 a.m. to 9 p.m., Sunday 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Each stall sets its own hours.
A short ride from Union Station, or about 15 minutes' walk from NoMa-Gallaudet Metro.

food.note: Many kitchens under one roof, so everyone finds something. Ask each stall about ingredients.

name: Ben's Chili Bowl
description: A U Street landmark since 1958, famous for its chili half-smoke. The original diner reopened in May 2026 after a long restoration, with its old counter and booths kept.
tips: Open until 4 a.m. on Friday and Saturday nights.
Across from the U Street Metro station.
Expect a line at busy times; it moves fast.

food.note: Ask which sausages and chili contain pork; the menu has other choices.

name: Georgetown and the C&O Canal
description: The city's oldest neighborhood: brick Federal houses, cobbled side streets, shops along M Street and a towpath beside the old canal, down to the river and the waterfront park.
tips: No Metro stop: walk from Foggy Bottom station, or take a bus or ride.
Walk the quiet residential streets north of M Street, then down to the waterfront.

access.note: Brick sidewalks and some steep streets up from the river.

name: The Wharf
description: A waterfront promenade with restaurants, piers and the Municipal Fish Market, a historic open-air seafood market. A good evening stroll.
tips: Free to walk. Waterfront Metro is a few minutes away.
Easy to pair with the Tidal Basin memorials, a walk to the west.

name: Arlington National Cemetery
description: The national military cemetery across the river: rows of white headstones, the Kennedy graves and the Changing of the Guard at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.
tips: Free. Open daily 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. from October to March.
The Changing of the Guard is every hour, on the hour, from October to March.
Metro Blue Line to Arlington Cemetery station, right by the welcome center.
An active cemetery with daily funerals: be quiet and respectful.
how: Metro Blue Line to Arlington Cemetery

access.note: Hilly and spread out. A paid tram tour saves the walking.

name: Old Town Alexandria
description: An 18th-century river town of brick rowhouses, shops and restaurants along King Street, down to the Potomac waterfront.
tips: Take Metro to King Street-Old Town, then the free King Street Trolley down to the river.
The trolley runs every 15 minutes, 11 a.m. to 11 p.m., every day.
how: Metro Blue or Yellow Line to King Street-Old Town, then the free trolley

name: George Washington's Mount Vernon

price.text: $30 adults · $16 ages 6 to 11 · 5 and under free

lead_time: Buy tickets online for a good Mansion tour time.
description: George Washington's home and farm above the Potomac: the mansion, gardens, a working farm and the tombs of George and Martha Washington, with an honest look at the enslaved people who lived and worked here.
tips: Adults $30, ages 6 to 11 $16, 5 and under free. Parking is free.
Open every day of the year; 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. from November to March.
Buy online for the best Mansion tour time; on busy days the next tour can be hours away.
By public transport: Metro Yellow Line to Huntington, then the Fairfax Connector bus.
how: About 30 to 45 minutes by car or ride app; or Metro and bus

access.note: Gravel paths and a fair amount of walking between buildings.

name: Udvar-Hazy Center (Air and Space)
description: Air and Space's giant hangars near Dulles airport: Space Shuttle Discovery, an SR-71 Blackbird, a Concorde and hundreds of aircraft.
tips: Free, no passes needed. Open 10 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. daily except Dec 25.
Parking is $15, free after 4 p.m.
Good on the way to or from a flight at Dulles.
how: By car or ride app, about 10 minutes from Dulles airport
